chunks: My father (ra) through Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah, from Mu'awiya ibn Hukaym, from Mu'mar ibn Khallad, from Abul-Hasan al-Rida (AS), from his father, who said:
Abu 'Abdullah (AS) stated: 'The salvation of a believer lies in safeguarding his tongue.' And Amir al-Mu'minin (AS) said: 'Whoever safeguards his tongue, Allah will conceal his faults.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of guarding one's tongue in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Thawab al-A'mal, transmitted through the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt, underscores the tongue as the primary instrument of both spiritual ruin and salvation, a concept central to Shia ethical theology (akhlaq). By linking the preservation of speech to the concealment of one's 'awrah' (faults or sins), it highlights how verbal discipline serves as a shield against divine exposure of one's inner state, reinforcing the practical application of taqwa in daily conduct.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: From my father (ra) through Saʿd ibn ʿAbdullāh, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaim, from Muʿammar ibn Khallād, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā (AS), from his father, who said that Abū ʿAbdullāh (AS) stated:
"The salvation of a believer lies in safeguarding his tongue." And Amīr al-Muʾminīn (AS) said: "Whoever safeguards his tongue, Allah will conceal his faults."
